chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who recites, in the obligatory prayer, the Opening of the Book and another surah in a single breath. He said: 'If he wishes, he recites in one breath, and if he wishes, in another.'

key_terms.فَاتِحَة الْكِتَاب: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: Can I recite Surah Al-Fatiha and another Surah in one breath during obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), this hadith highlights the juristic flexibility (rukhsah) in recitation during obligatory prayers, allowing the worshipper to choose between reciting Al-Fatiha and an additional surah in one breath or dividing them. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on ease and removing hardship for the congregant, accommodating varying physical capacities during the standing (qiyam) portion of the prayer. It underscores the principle that the validity of the prayer is not contingent upon rigid uniformity in recitation speed, provided the essential components are fulfilled.
